title: Chapter 63 — The Crotch
paragraphs: Out of the trunk, the branches grow. Out of them, the twigs. So, in productive subjects, grow the chapters.

The crotch mentioned on a previous page deserves separate attention. It is a notched stick of a particular form, about two feet long, which is inserted vertically into the starboard gunwale near the bow. It serves as a rest for the wooden end of the harpoon, whose other naked, barbed end projects at an angle from the bow, like a lean branch from a bare tree. The harpoon lies there like a tomahawk or any other weapon handy for instant use. Two harpoons typically rest in the crotch — one for the first throw, the other as a backup.

But these two harpoons, each by its own cord, are both connected to the line. The purpose is this: to throw them both, if possible, one right after the other into the same whale, so that if one should pull out during the drag, the other may still hold. It doubles the chances. But it very often happens that, owing to the confused whale-line in the boat at the time of a fast run, the second harpoon gets tangled up and cannot be thrown. The very tension of the line sometimes prevents the boatman from clearing it.

Furthermore: you should know that when the second iron is thrown overboard, it from that point becomes a dangling, sharp-edged terror, skittishly dancing about both boat and whale, tangling the lines or cutting them, and causing a prodigious commotion in all directions. Nor, in general, is it possible to recover it until the whale is fairly captured and a slack line obtained.

Consider now how it must be when four boats are all engaging one unusually strong, active, and intelligent whale — when, owing to these qualities and to the thousand coinciding accidents of such a daring enterprise, eight or ten loose second harpoons may be simultaneously dangling about him. For, of course, each boat is supplied with several harpoons to replace those that are lost in the fight, and some of these are sure to be thrown and go wild. Trapped in the tangle of lines and weapons, a right whale might almost say he is being attacked with darts.
